audits.title: Recognition session event contract, payload conversion, and minimum recording gate
notes: Recognition event reduction matches upstream: any Error event fails, the last FinalText wins, and Completed without Final/Error is a normal empty recognition rather than a backend failure.

Empty recognition returns an empty recognition payload, skips scene text postprocessing, and follows recording -> inferring -> idle without a postprocessing status; private D-Bus coverage proves the method reply and RecognitionResult carry the same empty payload.

Restored the upstream 8000 raw-sample minimum: shorter recordings cancel the session, return directly to idle, skip ASR/text finishing, and expose an exact empty StopRecording D-Bus reply without RecognitionResult.

Aligned streaming text projection so non-empty PartialText and early FinalText are emitted through RecognitionPartial during recording while early finals remain retained for stop-time payload construction and are not duplicated at stop.

Rust keeps a smaller typed BackendCapabilities shape because current upstream runtime decisions read only audio_delivery_mode; upstream supports_streaming, supports_partial_results, and requires_network are descriptor metadata without runtime consumers, while hotword capability is carried by model/provider metadata in both implementations.

The separate ERROR-INFO-001 audit now owns and implements frozen live RecognitionEvent::Error -> DaemonNotification classification; this recognition-contract unit remains non-overlapping and only owns event reduction/payload semantics.

audits.title: Recognition result JSON wire format and candidate source interpretation
notes: Daemon-produced raw/llm/asr recognition JSON, invalid-input fallback, commit-text normalization, and raw-candidate synthesis match the frozen upstream wire behavior.
Rust intentionally uses a typed CandidateSource: missing or unknown foreign source strings normalize to raw instead of preserving an arbitrary string; ordinary daemon-produced sources are unaffected.

Rust additionally preserves an empty cancel candidate and exposes RecognitionPayload::cancelled for typed frontend policy. The current Rust daemon does not produce that sentinel, and the frozen upstream defines kSourceCancel/menu handling but has no recognition-result producer for an empty cancel candidate.

audits.title: Core configuration schema, defaults, normalization, persistence, and validation
notes: Fixed dangling active ASR provider validation when the provider list is empty.
Validated input_gain in the upstream 0.1..10.0 range; Rust intentionally fails closed instead of clamping.
Rust scene provider omission remains an intentional extension because runtime provider resolution supports it.
Malformed/future-schema configs remain intentionally fail-closed.

audits.title: LLM command adapter process metadata and working-directory resolution
notes: Restored upstream args-first, command-second script-directory working-directory inference including ~/ expansion.
Explicit Rust working_dir remains a supported extension.
Fingerprint PID records, process groups, PID-reuse protection, and bounded TERM-to-KILL shutdown remain intentional safety enhancements.

audits.title: Scene/LLM post-processing, payload fallback, context, and OpenAI-compatible transport contract
notes: Aligned scoped vinput XML fallback tags, command fallback ordering, ASCII trimming, raw candidate retention, and recoverable LLM failure payloads.
Transport and prompt-file failures now preserve raw/selected+ASR payloads and emit typed warning notifications.
Context cache read failures are non-fatal like upstream.
OpenAI-compatible text connect attempts use the upstream 5-second maximum while scene timeout still bounds the full request.
Known gap: shutdown does not yet actively cancel an in-flight blocking OpenAI-compatible HTTP request; it waits for the request deadline.

audits.title: Prompt file loading and interpolation
notes: Unknown legacy double-brace placeholders remain verbatim.
Rust single-brace extensions no longer accidentally match double-brace legacy placeholders.

audits.title: Configured ASR backend selection and preparation
notes: Fixed local-provider dispatch to depend on type=local rather than the bundled sherpa-onnx provider id, matching upstream support for arbitrary stable local provider ids created by normal config/GUI flows.

Fixed local model backend selection so vinpst-model.json backend is authoritative exactly like upstream: missing/empty defaults offline, sherpa-offline selects offline, sherpa-streaming selects streaming, and unknown non-empty backend values fail closed; descriptive runtime metadata no longer overrides backend.
Command providers preserve the upstream id suffix rule: ids ending in .streaming use the streaming command backend and other command ids use batch mode.

Vinpst native OpenAI-compatible type=remote and the mock provider are intentional extensions beyond the frozen upstream factory; frozen upstream config variants are Local/Command and its browser remote service is a special command-provider path.

Rust build_active_prepared/prepare_backend consolidates warmup by creating and cancelling one session before swap. The corresponding upstream prepare/swap responsibility lives in recognition_session_manager and remains pending for its own non-overlapping audit.
Concrete model discovery/layout and native Sherpa implementation files are only supporting evidence here and remain pending for their dedicated model/backend audits.
Static configured ASR diagnostics now treat empty active_provider as a normal unselected state with empty last_error instead of reporting NoActiveProvider as a load failure.

audits.title: ASR session preparation, reload, and effective-backend state
notes: Fixed the valid empty active_provider state to match upstream disable semantics: startup and reload clear target/effective runtime ownership without treating the state as a backend-load failure, leave last_error empty, and future recording attempts fail only when a session is requested.

Reloading to an unselected provider while recording preserves the already-created active RecognitionSession but clears the effective backend for future sessions, matching upstream shared-backend session lifetime semantics.
Backend preparation still forces one CreateSession/cancel warmup before publication, matching upstream prepare-before-swap behavior.

Rust intentionally waits for Idle before preparing/applying a configured backend, whereas upstream can prepare/swap while a recording is active. This keeps runtime resource mutation outside busy recording/postprocessing phases.

Rust intentionally uses reload generations: stale prepared backends and stale failures are discarded, so an older request cannot be transiently published after a newer request arrives. Frozen upstream may briefly apply the earlier prepared backend before processing the later request.

Rust intentionally does not use the upstream BuildRuntimeSignature no-op optimization. Explicit reload requests therefore re-prepare even for apparently unchanged identity, which also avoids missing changes such as VAD thresholds/durations that the upstream signature does not include.
Reload success is silent and reload failure emits one notification in both implementations. Rust additionally suppresses stale-generation failure notifications.

Process-level --no-asr remains sticky across config reloads in both implementations. Rust intentionally exposes its disable reason through typed/D-Bus diagnostics; frozen upstream only reports that reason to stderr and leaves snapshot last_error empty.

Frozen upstream session snapshots use ResolvePreferredLocalModel even for non-local active providers, while Rust diagnostics report the active Command/Remote provider model. Exact legacy D-Bus state projection is deferred to the separate common/dbus ASR-state audit because the Rust projection file remains pending.

Upstream explicitly joins its reload thread during Shutdown. Rust owns reload work in Tokio tasks; async workers are cancelled with runtime shutdown while spawn_blocking preparation is waited by Tokio runtime teardown. No detached native preparation is intentionally created.

audits.title: Command ASR batch and streaming process protocols
notes: Fixed the main streaming gap: .streaming command providers now own one long-lived helper process across PushAudio calls instead of buffering all PCM until Finish. Intermediate chunks are sent with commit=false, the final pending chunk uses commit=true, and a finish control line closes input exactly like frozen upstream.

The daemon live poller now actively polls asynchronous streaming sessions on every tick, so helper stdout produced after PushAudio returns can reach RecognitionPartial before StopRecording. Early FinalText remains retained for the final payload and is not duplicated at stop.

Streaming JSON event handling matches upstream for session_started/empty/unknown no-ops, trimmed partial/final/final_timestamps text, duplicate-partial suppression, blank error fallback, closed completion, and malformed JSON fail-closed behavior.

Streaming cancel best-effort starts the helper, sends a cancel control event, emits Completed, and terminates the helper process group; tests prove descendant cleanup. Buffered command cancel now also emits Completed and buffered Finish is idempotent like upstream.

Batch command providers continue to write raw signed-16 little-endian PCM and use trimmed stdout as final text. On supported little-endian Linux targets this matches upstream native i16 byte transport.

Vinpst intentionally retains stronger process safety than frozen upstream: command helpers run in their own process group, direct-child exit cleans descendants, and stdout/stderr are independently capped at 1 MiB. Frozen upstream batch/streaming collectors have no comparable output cap and do not isolate a process group.

Frozen upstream streaming ignores provider timeout_ms and uses a fixed 10 second final wait with unbounded recording-stage pipe waits. Vinpst uses the same 10 second default when timeout_ms is absent, but an explicitly configured timeout bounds each streaming pipe write and final wait without imposing one whole-session deadline, so long recordings are not killed merely because their duration exceeds the provider timeout.

Existing Vinpst batch/JSON one-shot semantics intentionally keep timeout_ms=None as no configured deadline; managed provider materialization supplies 60000 ms. Frozen upstream leaves an omitted timeout at integer zero, which can immediately expire its batch helper deadline. This pre-existing safer behavior is preserved rather than copying the zero-timeout edge case.

The former one-shot LegacyCommandStreamingRunner is now test-only protocol coverage; production factory wiring uses LegacyCommandStreamingBackend. The .streaming suffix remains the authoritative selector and registry validation already requires stream metadata to agree with that suffix.
Live RecognitionEvent::Error -> DaemonNotification classification is now completed by the separate ERROR-INFO-001 audit; this command unit continues to own helper protocol/process semantics only.

audits.title: Native Sherpa offline and streaming recognition runtime
notes: Fixed native PCM scaling to divide signed i16 samples by 32768.0 for both offline and online recognizers, matching frozen upstream full-scale normalization.

Fixed native session lifecycle parity: repeated Finish is idempotent, Cancel is idempotent and yields Completed, and a completed recognizer with no text is a normal empty recognition rather than a backend error.
Restored upstream result extraction fallback: non-empty result.text wins; otherwise concatenated result.tokens are trimmed and used for offline results, online partials/endpoints, and final results.

Fixed online endpoint behavior: after each decode step, endpoint detection emits any changed hypothesis before resetting the stream, then decoding continues. Endpoint reset does not invent an application-level final/commit; push-to-talk still finalizes on StopRecording.
Fixed stop-time online projection so a final hypothesis that differs from the last emitted partial is first emitted as PartialText and then FinalText, exactly matching frozen upstream.

Model hotwords are now gated by top-level supports_hotwords. Provider hotwords override model hotwords, unsupported models ignore them at runtime, and an effective hotword path forces modified_beam_search for both offline and online recognizers.

Added all frozen-upstream online families supported by the sherpa-onnx Rust binding: transducer, zipformer2_ctc, paraformer, nemo_ctc, and t_one_ctc, with path-level metadata tests and native-feature compilation.

Aligned thread policy: offline metadata defaults to 4 threads when omitted while explicit offline model metadata may override it; online runtime uses the frozen upstream runtime default of 4 threads rather than model metadata.
All frozen offline family mappings are now owned and completed by ASR-MODEL-001; this runtime unit retains only recognizer/session behavior ownership.

Known gap: frozen upstream can supply model tokens and hotwords through in-memory tokens_buf/hotwords_buf JSON byte strings. The later model-manager audit verified that sherpa-onnx 1.13.3 safe high-level OfflineModelConfig/OnlineModelConfig does not expose those C-API fields, so Vinpst keeps the gap explicit rather than adding raw unsafe FFI.
Model path discovery/layout inference and VAD remain supporting evidence only and stay pending for their own non-overlapping audits.

audits.title: Offline Silero VAD trimming
notes: Silero detector construction matches frozen upstream: 16 kHz, 512-sample window, threshold/min-speech/min-silence controls, max speech duration 0, one CPU thread, debug disabled, and a 30 second detector buffer.

VAD config defaults are exactly aligned at enabled=true, threshold=0.45, min_speech_duration=0.15, min_silence_duration=0.5, and speech_pad_ms=300; config-level and resolved-plan tests pin the mapping so the two duration fields cannot be swapped.

Trim behavior matches upstream for reset, exact 512-sample feeds, zero-padding the final partial window, flush, segment extraction, independent per-segment speech padding, concatenation including overlapping padded regions, and returning original audio when no speech is found.

VAD model resolution intentionally differs from the frozen compile-time VINPUT_VAD_MODEL_PATH: Vinpst supports an explicit VINPST_SHERPA_VAD_MODEL, user/system XDG data locations, and a development asset. Missing/unloadable VAD still fails open to untrimmed audio like upstream.

Vinpst intentionally adds a 500 ms cold-start guard for the first detected segment: if its padded start lies within the first 500 ms, trimming preserves audio from sample zero to reduce first-syllable clipping after capture startup. Frozen vad_trimmer.cpp has no equivalent guard.

Frozen upstream initializes the detector at 16 kHz and ignores the sample_rate argument passed to Trim. Vinpst production capture is likewise 16 kHz, but injected/non-16-kHz PCM explicitly bypasses VAD instead of running a 16-kHz detector against mismatched-rate samples.
VAD remains offline/buffered only in both implementations; online/streaming Sherpa recognition does not use this trimmer.

audits.title: Installed ASR model discovery, metadata, layout, and removal
notes: Audited frozen installed-model discovery, metadata/path validation, runtime-language hints, model validation/removal safety, and native Sherpa family asset mapping without absorbing live registry network/schema ownership.

Fixed metadata path containment for offline and online Sherpa assets, including parent and symlink escapes; managed removal now rejects symlink targets and verifies canonical root containment while retaining Vinpst active-model protection.

Fixed native model coverage and metadata semantics: all 19 frozen offline families and all five frozen streaming families are accepted, including nemo_transducer family-keyed assets, Moonshine v2 encoder+merged-decoder layouts, frozen Qwen3/FunASR defaults, Whisper timestamp flags, and frozen RuntimeLanguageHint behavior.

Installed discovery now preserves malformed metadata entries as explicit broken models instead of failing the whole catalog; CLI reports broken state, daemon target menus exclude broken models, and GUI semantic state disables Use while keeping removal available.
Intentional Vinpst extensions remain: flat managed-model discovery in addition to the frozen two-level layout, a moonshine_v1 compatibility alias, and stronger active-model/symlink removal guards.

Remaining dependency gap: frozen tokens_buf/hotwords_buf in-memory Sherpa metadata cannot be represented through sherpa-onnx 1.13.3 safe Rust Offline/Online model configs; normal crates remain unsafe-free rather than bypassing the binding with raw FFI.

audits.title: Daemon error classification and notification payloads
notes: Ported the frozen daemon ClassifyErrorText taxonomy into one crate-private classifier preserving code, subject, detail, raw-message, prefix recursion, nested provider/model adoption, model/audio/D-Bus failures, LLM/HTTP processing failures, prompt-file URI parsing, and unknown fallback.

D-Bus emission now uses the classifier for recording-start failures, live streaming RecognitionEvent::Error, stop-time ASR failures, text postprocess failures, and current-generation ASR reload failures. Live Error events are drained in event order while the session retains its fatal state, so Stop produces no fabricated text and does not duplicate an already-emitted notification.

Private-session D-Bus evidence proves exact daemon_busy and asr_provider_timeout ssss payloads, live notification before Stop, stop-time notification before the operation failure, and bounded no-duplicate behavior. The complete daemon lib suite and 19 private-bus integration tests pass under strict dbus-integration Clippy.

The frozen header also defines daemon_start_failed and daemon_restart_failed, but frozen generation occurs only in cli/runtime/systemd_client.{cpp,h}, not error_info.cpp. The corresponding Rust CLI daemon-control files remain pending and do not yet project those two structured codes; that cross-module gap stays assigned to the later CLI-service audit rather than creating unused daemon constants.
